runtime_status: runtime-evidenced on Windows PowerShell 5.1: every MCP server in three live provider configs completed a real initialize -> tools/list exchange, and the three dead command paths found there were repaired and re-verified. Linux/static/artifact gates pass in CI.
notes: v7.9.6: the capability profiles shipped in 7.9.5 were project-DETECTED and machine-REGISTERED. Every profile in PROFILES.json carried "scope": "global", so enabling one for a single project put its servers into the machine-wide config of every provider and left them there until someone ran -Disable by hand -- the exact cost the router was built to avoid, and directly contradicted by CATALOG.json's own "NOT registered globally" note. It was found the only way it can be found: by a user noticing the context bill and turning code-deep off manually. Fixed by writing each profile where only its project can see it. Each provider's mechanism was verified against the installed CLI rather than recalled: Claude Code 2.1.237 takes projects["<abs path>"].mcpServers in ~/.claude.json (where `claude mcp add --scope local` writes, confirmed by reading it back with `claude mcp list` from that directory) -- preferred over the project's .mcp.json because it leaves no file in the user's repository and raises no trust prompt; grok 1.0.5 takes <project>/.grok/config.toml (`grok mcp add -s project`); codex-cli 0.147.0 has no project scope at all, proven by placing a .codex/config.toml in a project and finding it absent from `codex mcp list` run there; kimi-code showed no project pickup under `kimi doctor`; `hermes mcp add` has no scope option. Those three are skipped with the reason printed rather than written machine-wide behind a comment claiming otherwise, and -Global is the explicit opt-in. code-deep is renamed code-intel (the old id still resolves) because the name promised depth it never had -- it holds one server. Serena is told which project with --project <path>, verified against the installed Serena 1.7.0's own --help; a -Global registration gets --project-from-cwd instead, because one baked absolute path in a machine-wide config would activate that project in every unrelated session. State migrates from the flat v1 shape to a per-project v2, and the upgrade MOVES the old machine-wide entries rather than renaming them in a state file: it removes them from every provider config, then re-registers for the project the state recorded, touching only ids this pack recorded as enabled. Building it surfaced four more defects, all reachable by users: Get-ClaudeDesktopConfigPath crashed whenever [Environment]::GetFolderPath returned the empty string it documents for a folder that does not exist, so Join-Path took the whole run down inside a helper whose only job was to answer 'is Claude Desktop installed'; `uv tool install serena-agent` prints 'already installed' on stderr and exits 0, which under $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop' killed the auto-install on every re-run -- the success path treated as fatal; an identical rewrite counted as a change, taking a timestamped .bak file inside the user's project on every install run; and -Disable with no -Path defaulted to the current directory, sweeping a directory nobody asked about while leaving the real registrations in place. The Grok ceiling now counts the union of the user and project config files, because grok-cli runs both. TESTS/Test-McpProfiles.ps1 gained 49 checks that drive the real front-end script against a sandboxed USERPROFILE, LOCALAPPDATA and APPDATA and then read the resulting provider configs -- clean install, detected project, unrelated project, repeated runs, -CheckOnly, -Global, -Disable, the 7.9.5 migration, a recorded project that no longer exists, and the budget. Every one of them would have failed against 7.9.5. 144 canonical skills across 5 provider trees, unchanged: this release is capability routing and context cost, not skill count.
